subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmeai.com>, Tom Park <tom.park@acmeai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Sarah / Tom 1

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we all have the same baseline and clear next steps. If anything below is off, flag it and Ill update.

Key pain points you shared:
- High tail latency during peak traffic bursts (3rd-party search + chat mix) causing poor UX and timeouts in the mobile app.
- Current infra limits ability to scale GPU-backed inference without major rework and cost spikes.
- Concern about data residency and auditability for user logs/embeddings.

Customer goals / success criteria (discussed today):
- Latency: 95th percentile single-turn response <= 250ms for standard chat path (max prompt 1k tokens) under expected peak of 150 QPS.
- Throughput: sustained 200 QPS for embeddings/async batch jobs with burst to 400 QPS for short windows.
- Cost target: reduce per-request GPU cost by ~30% vs current deployment.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and customer-managed KMS for PII-sensitive tokens.

Technical notes from the call (what we heard):
- Model: planning to use a 13B open model (quantized) for chat; occasional fallback to a 7B variant for non-critical flows.
- KV cache behavior: long short-term conversational contexts (up to 8k tokens) with many repeated prefixes 1 prefix/KV caching will matter.
- Topology preference: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with private VPC peering; possible on-prem evaluation for regulated customers.
- Autoscaling: want predictable autoscale (warm pools) rather than cold start scale-ups.

Attachments Im sharing: SLO-draft.pdf (initial SLO table), deployment-topology.png (suggested topology with dedicated pools + fallback), prefix-caching-notes.docx (cache behavior and expected savings).

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) Redwood: produce a short performance runbook + proposed topology diagrams by Thu 31 Mar (owner: me).
2) Acme: provide representative traffic trace + 24h spike period (owner: Sarah) 1 target Mon 05 Apr.
3) Joint: schedule infra deep-dive with Acme SREs to validate VPC/peering and throughput tests 1 owner: Aditya to coordinate.

Longer-term evaluation plan we discussed: run small-scale perf tests with the 13B quantized model on dedicated nodes, compare latency/throughput tradeoffs with 7B fallback, evaluate intelligent batching + prefix caching to reduce token cost.

Appreciate the time today 1 Ill follow up with the performance runbook and a calendar invite for the SRE deep-dive.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference

Marissa 1

Thanks for the thorough recap. That matches our notes and is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 150 QPS peak number was specific to our chat-critical path only; for embeddings/async jobs the 200 QPS sustained is correct (higher concurrency due to batch sizes).
- For the 95th <= 250ms target, can you call out whether that assumes warm cache + 1 GPU shard per replica? We want to ensure apples-to-apples for your perf tests.

Ill upload the traffic sample to the Drive link you shared by Mon 05 Apr. Tom (copied) will join the SRE deep-dive 1 hes our infra lead.

One more ask: can we also get a short note on expected cost delta between dedicated pool vs hosted autoscale for our usage profile? Even a ballpark will help procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah
